---
title: "Query a database table"
---

Summarize 2013's hourly weather at the three New York City airports in an
SQLite table, with phibble's methods compiled to one SQL query that the
database runs. The table holds nycflights13's `weather` data from the
[PHPstats datasets](https://github.com/phpstats/datasets#weather): the
script reads the CSV and loads five columns into an in-memory SQLite
database before the code shown. It needs the pdo_sqlite extension.

- Each airport has about 8,700 hourly readings with a temperature.
- Newark (EWR) had the most precipitation, 43.8 inches over the year, and JFK
  the least, 34.7 inches. Mean temperatures differ by about 1 °F, and JFK had
  the strongest gust, 66.7 mph.
- `max(..., na_rm: true)` skips the hours without a gust; `mean()` and
  `sum()` need no `na_rm` here, because the filter keeps only hours with a
  temperature and every such hour has a precipitation value.
- Table methods only build the query. Nothing runs on the database until
  `collect()` returns a `DataFrame`. `showQuery()` shows the SQL with `?`
  placeholders.
- The same code runs on PostgreSQL and MySQL.

Runnable scripts: [PHP 8.5+](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phpstats/phibble/main/docs/examples/database-table.php)
· [PHP 8.3–8.4](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phpstats/phibble/main/docs/examples/database-table-chain.php).
